the_census_repair.defect: the subcommand candidate reader kept only the FIRST column of a line, and openssl prints its commands as a columnar table -- `req  rsa  rsautl` -- so the command that CREATES a certificate was never a candidate at all
the_census_repair.second_defect: DEFAULT_MAX_SUBCOMMANDS was 24, an underived number that read 24 of openssl's 147 commands; `req` sits at index 37, so even after being made a candidate it was cut before it was asked
the_census_repair.cost_of_removing_the_cap: 0.7 s for openssl to ask all 147; no measurable cost for any other program in the fleet; admission is decisive and refuses prose, so the cap bought no safety either

examples: openssl req -x509 -newkey=rsa:1024 -keyout=produced.key -out=produced.pem -days=1 -nodes -subj=/CN=produced  -> exit 0, both files produced
consumer_accepts: openssl x509 -in=produced.pem -out=out.bin : exit 1 -> 0 and the tree changes
why: 141 ask for a `key`, and the operations asking are `ca`, which reads its key from `openssl.cnf` and never from the file produced -- the artefact is present and unused
92 ask for a `certificate`; the ones that name a file need it in the form THAT operation declared, not the form the producer chose
24 ask for `parameters`; dhparam needs an input it does not have, so its producer exits 1 and status is UNVERIFIED rather than credited

the_guard_that_is_the_real_contribution.frontier_measurement: arXiv 2611.23305 (Dependency Fabrication in Repository Deployment Agents): probe repositories with a dependency that cannot legitimately be obtained; Repo2Run and SetupX agents almost always fabricated a stub and the harnesses MOSTLY MARKED THE RUN SUCCESSFUL; rules in the prompt or in CONTRIBUTING.md did not reliably prevent it
our_three_conditions: PRODUCED, NOT WRITTEN: the producer is composed only from flags the program printed, checked against the subcommand's OWN scope; this module never assembles artefact bytes
VERIFIED BY THE PROGRAM: the consumer that refused is re-run and must accept; a stub cannot pass because openssl refuses bytes that are not a certificate
NO VANISHING: the artefact must survive and the tree must have changed
the_guard_that_is_the_real_contribution.adversarial_check: a stub named produced.pem with PEM armour and no content: openssl x509 exit 1, 'Could not read certificate from produced.pem'
the_guard_that_is_the_real_contribution.adversarial_key_check: a stub produced.key: openssl pkey exit 1, 'Could not read key'

the_refusal_reader_repair.defect: the UNLOADABLE noun capture took everything after the verb, so `Could not open file or uri for loading certificate from in.txt` yielded the kind `file or uri for` and `Could not read certificate from in.txt` yielded `certificate from in` -- fragments no producer can be found for
the_refusal_reader_repair.fix: the kind is the noun the locative preposition hangs off: cut at from/into/at, drop the program's own loader words, keep the last noun
the_refusal_reader_repair.measured: 601 UNLOADABLE refusals on the enlarged openssl census now yield real kinds (key 141, certificate 92, parameters 24, crl, directory) instead of phrases

honest_limits: the manufacturer adds ZERO doors to the fleet; its genuine artefacts are used by the consumers that were tested directly, not by the refused operations
the census repair is what moved the doors (60 -> 174) and it is a reading repair, not a manufacturing one
the producer table is three kinds (certificate, key, parameters); every other kind is reported NO_DECLARED_PRODUCER rather than guessed at
openssl's `ca` reads its key from a config file, so a produced key cannot satisfy it; that is a real environmental dependency this module does not model
authority NONE, sandbox only; independent verification OPEN
no benchmark result is claimed: this round measured the census and the guard, not a task suite
